title: BOTTLE PLANTER
description: Turn a plastic bottle into a self-watering planter for windowsill herbs.
materialsNeeded: Cotton wick yarn or fabric strip
precautions: Smooth sharp plastic cut edges with sandpaper or masking tape.
Keep cutting tools angled away from your body.

steps.title: Section the plastic bottle
steps.instructions: Measure about 4 inches down from the neck and cut the bottle horizontally into two halves.

steps.title: Thread the capillary wick
steps.instructions: Pierce the cap and insert the cotton wick, leaving 3 inches hanging into the water reservoir.

steps.title: Plant soil & seed
steps.instructions: Invert the top funnel into the water base, fill with aerated soil, plant basil or mint seeds.

title: JAR LANTERN
description: Repurpose a glass jar as a warm fairy-light lantern for evenings.
materialsNeeded: 1 clean glass mason or sauce jar
1 battery/USB powered micro fairy light string (warm white)
Coarse sea salt or sand for bottom layer
Twine or copper wire for hanging handle
precautions: Ensure glass is crack-free before washing and assembling.
Keep battery pack dry and easily accessible under the lid.

steps.title: Prepare & sanitize glass jar
steps.instructions: Soak jar in warm soapy water to remove label adhesive. Dry thoroughly.

steps.title: Create diffuse glow base
steps.instructions: Pour 1 inch of clean sand or white salt into the base to disperse the lower LED beams.

steps.title: Thread lights & secure lid
steps.instructions: Coil the fairy wire naturally inside the jar, tape the mini switch underneath the lid, and seal.

title: CARDBOARD DESK ORGANIZER
description: Corrugated cardboard becomes a modular desk organizer.
materialsNeeded: PVA craft glue or glue stick
precautions: Always cut against a non-slip metal straight edge on a cutting mat.
Retract knife blade when not actively scoring cardboard.

steps.title: Score interlocking notches
steps.instructions: Cut 6 matching partition pieces with 3mm slots matching the cardboard flute thickness.

steps.title: Interlock compartments
steps.instructions: Slot vertical and horizontal panels together in a grid layout to create phone, pen, and notebook caddies.

steps.title: Reinforce edges & finish
steps.instructions: Apply a thin bead of wood glue along the base seam and seal raw corrugated edges with paint.

title: DENIM TOTE
description: Old jeans become a sturdy market tote in under an hour.
materialsNeeded: 1 pair of old or torn denim jeans
Sewing pins & sewing needle or machine
precautions: Use heavy-duty denim needles (size 16) to avoid breaking on thick seams.
Wear eye protection when stitching through reinforced belt loops.

steps.title: Cut denim legs horizontally
steps.instructions: Cut straight across both legs right below the crotch. Retain top portion for main tote.

steps.title: Double-stitch bottom seam
steps.instructions: Turn inside-out, pin bottom edge together, and run a durable double straight stitch.

steps.title: Create shoulder straps
steps.instructions: Cut two 2.5-inch strips from leftover pant legs, fold inward, stitch, and anchor firmly to the waistband.

title: TIN CAN LAMP
description: Punch a pattern into a tin can to cast beautiful light patterns.
materialsNeeded: Cleaned steel soup or vegetable cans
Freezer with water (to prevent can denting)
LED tea light or votive candle
precautions: Freeze water inside can solid before hammering to maintain rigid round cylinder shape.
File any sharp interior edges around the rim before inserting candle.

steps.title: Fill with water and freeze
steps.instructions: Fill clean can with water up to half an inch from the rim and freeze overnight.

steps.title: Hammer punch pattern dots
steps.instructions: Tape your dot stencil onto the ice-filled can and tap nail points through the tin.

steps.title: Melt ice, dry, and illuminate
steps.instructions: Rinse under warm tap to melt the ice core, towel dry thoroughly, and place candle inside.

title: PALLET SHELF
description: Reclaim pallet wood into a rustic wall-mounted shelf.
materialsNeeded: Pry bar, hammer, and wood saw
precautions: Only use pallets stamped 'HT' (Heat Treated). Never use chemically treated (MB) pallets.
Wear work gloves to avoid splinters and safety goggles when sawing.

steps.title: Disassemble and measure slats
steps.instructions: Pry loose 4 top deck boards with pry bar and remove old nails completely.

steps.title: Sand smooth & trim to length
steps.instructions: Sand surfaces down to 220 grit to bring out the warm reclaimed grain, and saw to 24-inch shelf lengths.

steps.title: Join box shelf & mount
steps.instructions: Screw the backing and shelf ledges together, apply bees-wax or clear stain, and anchor securely into studs.
